checks.lead: Mirza Asadullah Beg Khan (27 December 1797 – 15 February 1869), commonly known as Mirza Ghalib, was an Indian poet and letter writer. Writing during the final years of the Mughal Empire and the rise of British colonial rule in India. He spent most of his life in poverty, and his poetry often addressed themes of love, loss, philosophy, the human condition, and socio-political disturbances with a depth and complexity that influenced the literary traditions of his time. He wrote in both Urdu and Persian. Although his Persian diwan (body of work) is at least five times longer than his Urdu diwan, his fame rests on his poetry in Urdu. His ghazals, noted for their intricate imagery and layered meanings, form a significant part of Urdu literature.
